en.headline: Hong Kong rises to 14th in Global Innovation Index 2026
en.dek: The city advanced one place among 139 economies and stayed fifth in Asia, with strong marks for credit, tertiary education and market sophistication, the World Intellectual Property Organization said.
body: Hong Kong climbed one place to 14th globally among 139 economies in the Global Innovation Index 2026 released by the World Intellectual Property Organization on Tuesday, remaining fifth in Asia.

Its ranking on the Innovation Input sub-index held steady at eighth worldwide, while the Innovation Output sub-index improved by one place to 21st. The government said it was pleased with the progress and reaffirmed that accelerating innovation and technology development is a policy priority.

Hong Kong scored above the high-income average on all five Innovation Input pillars. Market sophistication ranked second globally. Credit continued to top the world ranking, tertiary education placed third, and information and communication technology as well as investment both ranked fourth.

The government said it remains fully committed to building Hong Kong into an international innovation and technology centre in line with the directions set out in the city’s first Five-Year Plan, including the new paradigm of three major I&T parks and five key research and development institutions, plus the AI+ Initiative.

zh.headline: 全球創新指數香港升至第14位 亞洲保持第五
zh.dek: 世界知識產權組織公布2026年《全球創新指數》，香港在139個經濟體中再升一位至第14，亞洲維持第五，信貸繼續全球第一。
body: 世界知識產權組織周二公布2026年《全球創新指數》，香港在全球139個經濟體中排名再升一位至第14位，並在亞洲保持第五位。
在兩大副指數方面，香港「創新投入」維持全球第八，「創新產出」則升一位至第21位。政府表示樂見進展，並重申加快創新科技發展是政策優次。
香港在「創新投入」下五個支柱的得分均高於高收入經濟體平均值，當中「市場成熟度」全球第二。「信貸」繼續高踞全球第一，「高等教育」第三，「信息通信技術」及「投資」均第四。
政府表示會全力落實首份五年規劃方向，發展「三大創科園區及五大研發機構」新範式，並全面推進「人工智能+」計劃，致力將香港建成國際創科中心。
